versions.research_rationale:
EO 10057 (May 14, 1949, 14 FR 2585) transferred to the American Battle Monuments Commission the administration of fourteen World War II military cemeteries overseas, with supplies and cemetery records, effective cemetery by cemetery when the Army finished its operational mission and in no instance later than December 31, 1951 (paragraph 1); reserved the Army's right to re-enter the cemeteries for exhumations or reinterments after the transfer (paragraph 2); and provided a transfer of unexpended Army appropriation balances for use before a stated date (paragraph 3). I read the held Federal Register text layer (verified whole-order span) and the dossier inventory of three numbered paragraphs is complete. EO 10087 of December 3, 1949 (14 FR 7287, held Federal Register text) amended paragraphs 1 and 3 to read as set out; this is a strike-and-insert style rewrite, so paragraphs 1 and 3 continue as amended and EO 10087 is recorded as a later event with before and after text, not an end. Ends: paragraph 3 is a time-limited authority for the Director of the Bureau of the Budget; its own terms confine transfers to use before July 1, 1949 (original) and, after EO 10087, before July 1, 1950, so it is terminated by its own terms (recorded inclusive, 1949-06-30 for the original window; the exclusive reading is the start of July 1, 1949); EO 10087 re-set the window on December 3, 1949, after the first window had closed, and the second window closed on 1950-06-30 inclusive. No source held shows whether any balances were transferred, so no performance date is claimed. Paragraphs 1 and 2 have no end date or condition other than the paragraph 1 transfer timetable. Paragraph 1 is a performed, self-executing transfer whose per-cemetery effective dates are not held; its outer bound is 1951-12-31 and the allocation of administration to the Commission persists. Current predicate: the U.S. Code in force (36 U.S.C. 2111(b)(1)(A), held at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t36-s2111.txt, and the same section's notes, which set out EO 10057 as amended by EO 10087 as provided) refers to the duties and powers transferred to the Commission by EO 10057 as amended by EO 10087 and does not repeal them; the lookup shows the Code's four hits on this order, and the OFR-catalog search reports only EO 10087 and a mis-citation. The held Federal Register texts of EO 10087 and 10088 cite this order (10088 only prints on the same page). I found no revocation or supersession in the held orders. Route: original_plus_bounded_search with the amendment attached; the Code text is a continuation lead read by me, not a packet evidence record. Limit: the Code edition stops at 2026-10-09 and the held texts are Federal Register text layers. Nothing here is a certification.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The only own-terms ends are paragraph 3's use windows (before July 1, 1949, re-set by EO 10087 to before July 1, 1950) and the paragraph 1 outer date of December 31, 1951 for the transfers to take effect, which is a deadline for performance and not an end of the Commission's functions. EO 10087 amends and does not revoke; no other held order names EO 10057 (searched held texts: EO 10087, EO 10088 which only shares a page, the 1989 OFR snapshot and the Code). An earlier revocation or supersession is not shown.","independent_command_check":"Paragraph 2 depends on paragraph 1 only for the effective date of each transfer and is separately a standing Army right; it does not end with the paragraph 3 fund authority. Paragraph 1's supplies and records transfers are part of the same transfer command. The fund transfer in paragraph 3 is independent and time-limited.","savings_check":"No savings clause in the order; the savings description above records the accrued and transferred consequences and their sources. Nothing in the 2026-10-28 evidence ruling lets a later general rule end the surviving allocation of functions, and none was found.","scope_check":"Paragraph 1 (transfer of functions with supplies and records), paragraph 2 (Army re-entry right) and paragraph 3 (fund transfer) are distinct commands. The inventory excludes only the preamble authority recital (section 12 of the act of March 4, 1923) and the signature. EO 10087 touches paragraphs 1 and 3 only; paragraph 2 was never amended."}

The order has no express savings clause, and no source held shows the exact transfer or fund-transfer dates.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 10153 (Aug. 17, 1950, 15 FR 5492) prescribes under section 201(e) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949 the regulations on the travel time that counts as active duty for members of the uniformed services called to active duty for more than thirty days: section 1 (public transport schedules), section 2 (private conveyance: one day per 300 miles, fractions over 150 miles, not authorized when the call is under ninety consecutive days), section 3 (Secretaries may prescribe uniform supplementary regulations) and section 4 (effective September 1, 1950). I read the held Federal Register text layer (verified whole-order span 1214 to 3732). The dossier inventory was a single sole-paragraph clause; I replaced it with four section clauses (lead and section 1 together, section 2, section 3, section 4) at absolute character offsets of the held text so each section has its own state. Later events (both held as Federal Register texts): EO 10649 of Dec. 28, 1955 (20 FR 10095), effective January 1, 1956 under its paragraph 2, rewrote sections 1 and 2 (section 1 for travel from home to first duty station, section 2 for travel from last duty station to home, without regard to actual performance); EO 12683 of July 21, 1989 (54 FR 31162) rewrote section 1 into a single rule tied to allowable travel time and Secretaries' regulations, deleted section 2 and renumbered sections 3 and 4 as sections 2 and 3. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the rewrites of section 1 are amendments (recorded as later events with before and after text) and the clause continues; the deletion of section 2 is an express ending, dated July 21, 1989 (no delayed effective date appears in EO 12683; it was published July 26, 1989). Section 4 is an effective-date clause spent when the order took effect on 1950-09-01. Searches: number search of the held Federal Register order texts and the lookup show only EO 10649, EO 12683 and the 1989 OFR snapshot naming this order; the three bounded machine searches have 0 U.S. Code hits, 0 eCFR hits and 2 OFR-catalog hits (the two amendments). Route: original_plus_bounded_search, with both amendments attached. Limits: no current text of 37 U.S.C. 204(b) (cited by EO 12683 as authority) is held and the Code and eCFR searches name this order nowhere, so continuation rests on the absence of any held ending and on EO 12683 re-basing the authority in 1989; displacement by a later statute or unnumbered action cannot be excluded. The texts are Federal Register text layers, not page-checked images. Nothing here is a certification.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Section 2 ended by EO 12683's express deletion on 1989-07-21 (no earlier end shown; EO 10649 rewrote rather than ended it). Section 4 ended on its own date, 1950-09-01. Sections 1 and 3 have no own-terms end, and no held order revokes or supersedes EO 10153; EO 10649 and EO 12683 amend it and each says so. A search of the held orders for the number 10153 found no other citing order.","independent_command_check":"Section 3 (Secretaries' supplementary regulations) is independent of sections 1 and 2 and continues after section 2 was deleted; section 4's effective date is independent of the substantive sections and ended by arrival of the date. Section 1 and section 2 were separate commands: section 2 was removed in 1989 without ending section 1.","savings_check":"No savings clause in any of the three instruments; the 1989 deletion and rewrite are prospective amendments and the packet holds no source that preserves or removes earlier crediting, so no savings is claimed beyond the carried clauses.","scope_check":"Four sections, four scopes: lead with section 1, section 2, section 3, section 4. EO 12683's renumbering (old sections 3 and 4 become sections 2 and 3) is recorded as a later event of the surviving clauses and does not change which clause is which; the dossier's whole-order clause was replaced because it hid section 2's separate end."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order has no savings clause. Section 2's deletion by EO 12683 leaves the earlier-period travel time already credited as active duty untouched by any held source; no held source states a transition rule, so no pending right or accrued credit is claimed, and the surviving sections are carried as operative.

current_predicate.legal_basis: Continuing, amended, on the original_plus_bounded_search route: no own-terms end; EO 10649 (effective 1956-01-01) and EO 12683 (1989-07-21) amended section 1 without revoking it; no held order revokes or supersedes EO 10153; bounded searches name no ending. 37 U.S.C. 204(b), cited by EO 12683 as authority, is not held.

amendment: section 1 rewritten as a single rule tied to allowable travel time and the Secretaries' uniform regulations (EO 12683 paragraph 1)
amendment: section 2 rewritten as the rule for travel from last duty station to home without regard to actual performance (EO 10649 paragraph 1)

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10222 (16 FR 2247; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10222, Providing for Certain Transfers to the Federal Civil Defense Administration, signed March 8, 1951. Inventory: three numbered paragraphs, confirmed as three clauses: 1, transferring the civil-defense part of the health services and special weapons defense functions of the Health Resources Office of the National Security Resources Board to the Federal Civil Defense Administration, to remain under the Administrator's jurisdiction until further order of the President; 2, transferring related property, records and personnel; 3, effective as of March 4, 1951. Ending: section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919 of June 3, 1994 (59 FR 29525, held government printing) provides that Executive Order No. 10222 of March 8, 1951 (16 FR 2247) is superseded or revoked; the U.S. Code note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 note says the same and gives the date June 3, 1994. Section 904 has no stated effective date, so the end is read as effective on signing, 1994-06-03. Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10222 at 16 FR 2247, in the Federal Register of March 13, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10222, Providing for Certain Transfers to the Federal Civil Defense Administration, is signed March 8, 1951, and its filing line reads Filed, Mar. 12, 1951. Text and inventory: three numbered paragraphs, confirmed as three clauses. Paragraph 1 transfers to the Federal Civil Defense Administration so much of the health services and special weapons defense functions of the Health Resources Office of the National Security Resources Board as relates to civil defense, to remain under the jurisdiction of the Federal Civil Defense Administrator "until further order of the President." Paragraph 2 transfers the related property and records of the Board, and the personnel of the Health Resources Office engaged primarily in those functions, as the Board's Chairman and the Administrator jointly determine. Paragraph 3 reads "This order shall be effective as of March 4, 1951." Ending: Executive Order 12919, National Defense Industrial Resources Preparedness, signed June 3, 1994 and printed at 59 FR 29525 in the Federal Register of June 7, 1994 (held govinfo text layer), provides in section 904(a) that "The following are superseded or revoked:" and lists as item (2) "Executive Order No. 10222 of March 8, 1951 (16 FR 2247)". Neither section 904 nor any other part of that order states an effective date, so the end is dated on signing, 1994-06-03; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of June 7, 1994 is not used. The machine U.S. Code search found the editorial note under 42 U.S.C. 5195 that records the same revocation by section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919. versions.research_rationale: EO 10440 (March 31, 1953; 18 FR 1823-1824, read in the held govinfo scan) rewrote Civil Service Rule VI (secs. 6.1-6.6, creating Schedule C) and in sec. 2 directed the Commission to reclassify existing Schedule A and B positions, keeping them in place until it acted. Earlier events: EO 10463 (June 25, 1953) replaced sec. 6.4, so the original sec. 6.4 ended that day. The other Rule VI sections continued until EO 10577 sec. 301 revoked EO 10440 by name, effective (sec. 401) on the first Sunday after the sixtieth day after November 22, 1954, i.e. January 23, 1955, which is therefore the whole-order end (no later-ending clause exists). Sec. 2 is a transitional direction that was spent once the Commission had reclassified every listed position; the date that happened is not in the held sources, so its first end is left open rather than set to the revocation date. Savings: EO 10577's proviso carried the schedule listings into the new rules.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 10577 sec. 301 attaches a proviso to its revocations: positions listed in Schedules A, B and C 'as provided for in Civil Service Rule VI of that order, as amended' (that is, Rule VI as rewritten by EO 10440, which created Schedule C) 'shall be considered as being listed in Schedules A, B, and C, respectively,' of the new Rule VI, unless and until the Commission removes them. The Commission's schedule placements made under EO 10440 were therefore carried into EO 10577's schedules; they continue, if at all, under EO 10577 and later rules, not under EO 10440. No other savings clause was found.

Executive Order 10451 of 1953-04-28 (18 FR 2529; Federal Register Document 53-3883, filed 1953-04-30) orders that, until June 30, 1953, specified federal tax returns for periods through 1952 are open to inspection by the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives or a duly authorized subcommittee, in connection with the inquiry authorized by its resolution of January 27, 1953 into the administration of the Department of Justice and the Office of the Attorney General, subject to the conditions in the Treasury decision approved the same date. The held Federal Register text file contains this order followed by unrelated Civil Service Commission rules and a contents page from the same issue; the dossier's eleven clauses (including scopes labelled Schedule C, items and 633) were generated from those neighbouring documents, so the inventory is corrected to the single operative paragraph of the order. The order is a time-limited permission whose own wording fixes its end, so the terminating event is the stated until-date. Per the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on until-dates the end is recorded inclusive as 1953-06-30 (the order runs through that day); the alternative exclusive reading is that it ends when that day begins. No extension, amendment, revocation or supersession was found: the selected machine searches report none, and a search of all held order texts for the number 10451 and for inspection orders for this Committee finds only this order itself and orders for other committees or other periods.

versions.research_rationale: EO 10494 (signed 1953-10-14, 18 FR 6585), read in full from the held official FR text (pdfplumber reading-order recheck of PDF pages 3-4): preamble delegating 'the functions remaining under Title IV' of the Defense Production Act; sec. 1 ESA fiscal liquidation to the Treasury; sec. 2 Title IV administrative proceedings to the ODM Director; sec. 3(a)-(c) enforcement files, investigations and disallowance certification to the Attorney General; last paragraph: secs. 1-2 effective November 1, 1953, sec. 3 immediately. It has no term or sunset. EO 12148 sec. 5-103 revokes it 'as amended', effective 1979-07-15 under EO 12148 sec. 6. The dossier's 5 clauses cover the order from the enacting paragraph to the signature with no textual gap. D6 / earlier-end test: the OFR catalog records amendments by EO 10773 (1958) and EO 11051 (1962), a 'see' note from EO 11725 (1973) and the EO 12148 revocation; the USC note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 records the EO 12148 revocation. All three changing orders were read in the held FR texts and are attached as later events on sec. 2, the only clause naming the ODM Director: EO 10773 sec. 3 (ODM to OCDM, 1958-07-01), EO 11051 sec. 601(7) (OCDM to OEP, 1962-09-27) and EO 11725 sec. 3 item (5) (OEP authority under this order to GSA, 1973-07-01). None ends a clause. The OFR edge crediting EO 10494 with revoking EO 10332 is a page-sharing artifact: the revocation of EO 10332 is Part VI of EO 10495, printed next to it on the same page; it is not an act of this order. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_12148 (EO 12148, 44 FR 43239-43245, read once in full): sec. 6 makes the order effective July 15, 1979 although it was signed July 20, 1979, so the sec. 5-1 revocations take effect 1979-07-15; sec. 5-1 revokes thirteen orders 'as amended' without exception or delayed effect; the only continuation clause, sec. 2-302, lets the FEMA Director keep performing the functions transferred to him by sec. 1 'notwithstanding the revocations', which preserves FEMA's own transferred functions, not any provision of a revoked order; sec. 1-201 moves records, property, personnel and funds for the sec. 1 functions only. There is no pending-matter or savings clause for the revoked orders. Own-residual check, reading EO 10494 in full: it transferred the remaining Title IV (price and wage stabilization) functions of the Defense Production Act on the wind-down of the Economic Stabilization Agency: ESA fiscal liquidation to the Treasury Secretary (sec. 1), the conduct and conclusion of Title IV administrative proceedings to the ODM Director (sec. 2; later OCDM, OEP and, from 1973, GSA under EO 10773, 11051 and 11725), and the enforcement files, investigations and certification of disallowances to the Attorney General (sec. 3). Liquidation steps taken, proceedings concluded and disallowances certified before 1979-07-15 are completed acts under the transferred functions; EO 12148 does not undo them, and its sec. 2-302 continuation (FEMA's own functions) does not re-enact this order. No clause of EO 10494 continues; state transferred_or_accrued records the completed transfers and their effects. S1 transfer-wording prefill (review) resolved to transferred_or_accrued. Bounded search: the order and the ending instrument read in full; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held official FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals, every hit read in context); the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

Executive Order 10991 of 1962-02-06 (Federal Register Document 62-1426, filed 1962-02-08) is one paragraph signed by President Kennedy. Its only command amends Executive Order 10929 of March 24, 1961, which provides for a commission to consider a controversy between the carriers represented by the New York Harbor Conference Carriers' Committee and certain of their employees, by substituting a new second sentence in section 1 of that order: the commission is to consist of nine members, three from persons nominated by the carriers, three from persons nominated by the employees, and the chairman and two other members without nominations. The order states no effective date, so the amendment is treated as effective on signature. The selected machine searches report no instrument that revoked, superseded or amended Executive Order 10991. Held order texts that name number 10929 were also checked and none acts on Executive Order 10991.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11195 (30 FR 1169, Federal Register of February 4, 1965), signed by Lyndon B. Johnson and dated January 30, 1965; number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier's seven clauses (two amendment leads, four added positions and the effective-date sentence) cover every sentence of the order; I confirm them. Under section 303(g) of the Government Employees Salary Reform Act of 1964 the order amends Executive Order 11189 of November 23, 1964 by adding to its section 1 the Chief of Protocol, Department of State, as a Level IV position and to its section 2 three Level V positions (Staff Director, Commission on Civil Rights; Assistant Director (Program Planning, Analysis, and Research), Office of Economic Opportunity; General Counsel, Veterans Administration), and takes effect immediately. Ending: Executive Order 12060 (signed 1978-05-15) revokes this order by number in its section 3, and EO 11189 by the same sentence. The first end of every clause is that express revocation; amendments continue until the amended order ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments). Earlier candidate end that does not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; it is not the end because it does not name EO 11195): Pub. L. 89-554 (Sept. 6, 1966, 80 Stat. 378), which enacted title 5 of the United States Code, lists in 5 U.S.C. 5315 "(73) Chief of Protocol, Department of State." and in 5 U.S.C. 5316 item (101), the Assistant Director (Program Planning, Analysis and Research), Office of Economic Opportunity, "(110) General Counsel of the Veterans' Administration." and "(114) Staff Director, Commission on Civil Rights.", so every position this order added appears in the statute (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11195_Pub._L._89-554_Sept._6_1966_80_Stat._378_et_seq._including_5_U.S.C._5315_and_5316_as__c629b8a1e7.txt; it is not an evidence record of this dossier, so it is pinned here by path). The Federal Register catalog note on EO 11189 says that order was "Nullified by 80 Stat. 460, 461 (5 U.S.C. 5315, 5316)" because the statute included all positions added by EO 11189 and its amendment EO 11195 (jobs/later-events/output/CATALOG_INDEX.csv), but the catalog note on EO 11195 itself records only the EO 12060 revocation. Section 7(c) of the same Act provides that an order in effect under a replaced law continues in effect under the corresponding provision "until repealed, amended, or superseded.", which points the other way. I did not establish that the statute extinguished this order, so EO 12060 is recorded as the first end. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, whose hits for this order are the historical notes under 5 U.S.C. 5315 and 5316 and the 5 U.S.C. 5317 note stating that the order was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12060; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14, two machine hits without located text in the dossier, not relied on; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts, two machine hits, both recording the EO 12060 revocation); the number-citation scan of held order texts in the packet lookups, which found the number only in the texts of this order and of EO 12060; and a full read of EO 12060 (held Federal Register text, 1,871 characters). EO 12553 does not list 11195.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 11195 (1965-01-30, 30 FR 1169) amends EO 11189 of November 23, 1964 by adding to its section 1 the Chief of Protocol, Department of State, as an additional Level IV position and to its section 2 three additional Level V positions (Staff Director, Commission on Civil Rights; Assistant Director (Program Planning, Analysis and Research), Office of Economic Opportunity; General Counsel, Veterans Administration), under section 303(g) of the Government Employees Salary Reform Act of 1964, and takes effect immediately. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11195.txt, 30 FR 1169, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed its number, title and date against the census register. The dossier's seven clauses (two amendment leads, four added positions and the effective-date sentence) cover every sentence of the order, so I confirm the inventory. EO 12060 (signed 1978-05-15) revokes the order by number in its section 3, and the dossier carries the ACT record for it. The first end of every clause is that express revocation. Amendments continue until the amended order ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments, and EO 11189 was revoked by the same sentence. Earlier candidate end that does not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; it is not the end because it does not name EO 11195): Pub. L. 89-554 (Sept. 6, 1966, 80 Stat. 378), which enacted title 5 of the United States Code, lists in 5 U.S.C. 5315 the Chief of Protocol, Department of State, as item (73), and in 5 U.S.C. 5316 the Assistant Director (Program Planning, Analysis and Research), Office of Economic Opportunity as item (101), the General Counsel of the Veterans' Administration as item (110) and the Staff Director, Commission on Civil Rights as item (114), so every position this order added appears in the statute (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11195_Pub._L._89-554_Sept._6_1966_80_Stat._378_et_seq._including_5_U.S.C._5315_and_5316_as__c629b8a1e7.txt). The Federal Register catalog note on EO 11189 says that statute "Nullified by 80 Stat. 460, 461 (5 U.S.C. 5315, 5316)" EO 11189 and EO 11195 because it included all positions they added (jobs/later-events/output/CATALOG_INDEX.csv), but the catalog note on EO 11195 itself records only the EO 12060 revocation. Section 7(c) of the same Act says an order in effect under a replaced law continues in effect under the corresponding provision "until repealed, amended, or superseded", which points the other way. I did not establish that the statute extinguished this order, so EO 12060 is recorded as the first end. The 5 U.S.C. 5317 note in the U.S. Code release point also records that this order was revoked by EO 12060. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

versions.research_rationale: EO 11262 adds three items to EO 11248: in level IV, (4) Executive Secretary of the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice; in level V, (4) Director, Bureau of Outdoor Recreation and (5) Assistant to the Secretary of Defense (Legislative Affairs). No later amender deleted the two level V items (traced item by item through EO 11699); they ended with EO 11708 sec. 3 on March 23, 1973. EO 11409 item 1(b) formally deleted the level IV item on April 29, 1968. That position, however, belonged to a temporary commission: EO 11236 (held, 30 FR 9349) required the commission to report within 18 months and to terminate not later than 90 days after its report. The placement therefore probably lost its object before the 1968 deletion. Deadlines cannot fix the actual date, so that clause's first_end stays open. The whole-order end is unaffected because the two level V items ran to 1973-03-23. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. No human certification is asserted.

The only carve-out, EO 11708 sec. 3's exception for the positions listed in its sec. 2, does not cover them; EO 11768's incumbent clause (1974) concerns its own list.

EO 11587 (March 15, 1971) substitutes the words 'Commissioner, Water Quality Office, Environmental Protection Agency' for the original description, and EO 11604 (July 2, 1971) deletes item (8). versions.research_rationale:
EO 11367 (signed 1967-08-18, 32 FR 12037; held official Federal Register text read in full) adds item (5), 'Assistant Director for Executive Management, Bureau of the Budget, Executive Office of the President', to section 1 (level IV) of EO 11248. It has one operative sentence, a standing pay-level designation under 5 U.S.C. 5317, with no term or condition. The rest of the held extract (migratory-bird and other regulations on the same pages) is neighbouring material, not part of the order. Newly held: Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1970 (84 Stat. 2085-2086, read in full). Sec. 102(a) provides 'The Bureau of the Budget in the Executive Office of the President is hereby designated as the Office of Management and Budget'; sec. 102(b) designates the statutory Assistant Directors (31 U.S.C. 16a, 16c) Assistant Directors of OMB; sec. 103 makes the Bureau's records, property and personnel OMB's. That is a redesignation of the same entity and offices, so it abolishes nothing and is not an end. The Statutes at Large marginal note gives 'Effective July 1, 1970' for the plan, and sec. 301 sets July 1, 1970 as the floor; no end date in this claim depends on that note. EO 11540 (signed 1970-07-01, 35 FR 10735; held, read in full) states 'This order shall be effective July 1, 1970' and substitutes, in item (5), 'Assistant Director, Office of Management and Budget, Executive Office of the President' for the words of this order. I treat that as a conforming retitle, recorded as a later event and not as the first end: the item keeps its number and level IV, and the substituted title covers every OMB Assistant Director, including any post that was the former Assistant Director for Executive Management, so the placement was widened and renamed, not withdrawn. The dossier has no OMB organization record (the request was answered with the plan only); the judgment does not need one because the retitled item has a live object under sec. 102(b). The first end is EO 11708 (signed 1973-03-23, 38 FR 7979; held, read in full), sec. 3: 'Except with respect to the positions enumerated in section 2 of this order, Executive Order No. 11248 of October 10, 1965, as amended, is hereby revoked.' EO 11708 states no effective date or delay, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1973-03-23. Sec. 2 continues only eight level V positions, none of them OMB, so item (5) (level IV) is revoked; sec. 1(9) of EO 11708 places 'Assistant Director, Office of Management and Budget' in level IV under its own authority, a new placement and not a residue of this order. The three machine searches (U.S. Code release 119-121 and eCFR as of 2026-10-14: 0 hits; OFR disposition catalog: hits read, all EO 11540/11708) carry no coverage warning. A reviewer should test (a) whether EO 11540's substitution should be the first end instead (1970-07-01), and (b) whether the revocation date 1973-03-23 is right given EO 11708 has no effective-date wording.

versions.research_rationale: EO 11409 has five operative items. In level IV of EO 11248 it (1a) replaces item (3), the Food-for-Peace Special Assistant, with the Administrator, SRS; (1b) replaces item (4), the crime commission's Executive Secretary, with the Administrator, NIH; and (1c) adds (8) the Administrator, HSMHA and (9) the Executive Director, Cabinet Committee on Price Stability. In level V it (2) replaces item (15), the Administrator, SRS, with the Deputy Administrator, HSMHA. Items (3), (4), (8) and (15) survived every later amender and ended with EO 11708 sec. 3 on March 23, 1973. EO 11708 sec. 1 places the first three positions anew by its own authority; none is a sec. 2 exception. EO 11468 formally deleted item (9) on May 10, 1969. The committee was an ad hoc body, and no held source shows when it was discontinued, so that clause's first_end stays open. The whole-order end is 1973-03-23 in any case. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. No human certification is asserted.

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 11417 (33 FR 10625, July 24, 1968; the held extract also carries unrelated neighbouring rules): one sentence amending sec. 305 of EO 10973 of Nov. 3, 1961, 'as amended', by adding the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Domestic and International Business to the Development Loan Committee; no own term and no savings clause, and its operative effect exists only as text of EO 10973. I read the held full text of EO 12163 (44 FR 56673, Sept. 29, 1979) including secs. 1-902 to 1-905: sec. 1-903(a)(1) provides 'The following are revoked: (1) Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3, 1961, as amended', which removes the base order, with all its amendments (EO 11417 among them), from force, and sec. 1-905 makes it effective October 1, 1979. EO 11417 is not individually named in EO 12163, and the machine-selected ACT: spans for EO 12163 are wrong passages (allocation and references provisions) so I do not cite them; the basis is my reading of the actor text. Sec. 1-904 saves earlier delegations, determinations, regulations and similar actions 'made, issued, or entered into with respect to any function affected by this order' until amended or terminated; I read that as preserving executed administrative actions under the foreign-assistance functions, not the Development Loan Committee membership amendment, which is a rule of the revoked order's text, but this is a judgment recorded as a residual risk. The catalog note ('Revoked by: EO 12163, September 29, 1979') and 1989 row ('Revoked by EO 12163') agree but are leads only. Other machine-found chain orders (EO 11579, 11685, 11816, 11959, 12118) amend or supersede parts of EO 10973 and cannot end EO 11417 on their own. Provisional NO hypothesis only; the effective end (Oct. 1, 1979 per sec. 1-905) is not otherwise adjudicated.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (33 FR 10625, issue of July 26, 1968) is Executive Order 11417, adding an Assistant Secretary of Commerce to the membership of the Development Loan Committee. I read the whole order, a single operative paragraph: Executive Order No. 10973, as amended, "is hereby further amended by inserting in section 305" the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Domestic and International Business. The held text layer also carries neighbouring Commerce regulations on the same pages, which are not part of the order. End: the parent was revoked by Executive Order 12163, effective October 1, 1979, Executive Order 12163 (signed September 29, 1979; 44 FR 56673) states in section 1-903(a) that the following are revoked: "(1) Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3,1961, as amended;" and in section 1-905 "The provisions of this order shall become effective as of October 1,1979." Its section 1-505 establishes a Development Loan Committee and its section 1-506 a Development Coordination Committee, which are new committees under that order and are not treated as keeping this order in force. Executive Order 11579 section 4(d) (1971) supersedes Executive Order No. 10973 only insofar as provisions conflict; it names no section of this order's insertion and no source shows it extinguished the amendment, so it is not an end. The amendment lived only as text inside section 305 of the parent, so it ended with the parent on 1979-10-01. Other held amendments of the parent (Executive Orders 11685, 11816, 11959 and 12118) were checked and do not mention section 305 or this insertion; Executive Order 11841 adds a different section 306. The machine search lists these as chain items only.

versions.research_rationale: EO 11468 (1) replaces level IV item (9), the Executive Director of the Cabinet Committee on Price Stability, with the Deputy Under Secretary for International Labor Affairs, and (2) adds level V items (23) Deputy Assistant Postmaster General, Bureau of Operations and (24) Director, Office of Minority Business Enterprise. Item (9) was renumbered (8) by EO 11581 and ended with EO 11708 sec. 3 on March 23, 1973; EO 11708 sec. 1(12) places the same position anew. Item (24) was replaced by EO 11516 on March 19, 1970. Item (23) was renumbered and then formally deleted by EO 11634 on December 6, 1971. Before that, however, the Postal Reorganization Act (Pub. L. 91-375) abolished the Post Office Department, whose positions the 5 U.S.C. 5315 notes show it struck. That earlier statutory end is probable but not dated in held sources, so that clause's first_end stays open. The whole-order end is 1973-03-23 in any case. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. No human certification is asserted.

The order establishes the Ohio River Basin Commission (Section 1), fixes its jurisdiction (Section 2) and membership (Section 3: a Chairman, Federal agency members, State members and interstate agency members), its functions (Section 4) and a reporting section (Section 5). First end: Section 5(a)(4) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11578, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. EO 11659 (Establishment of the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission), signed 1972-03-22. The order establishes the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission (Section 1), fixes its jurisdiction (Section 2) and membership (Section 3), functions (Section 4), consultation with adjoining States (Section 5) and reporting (Section 6). Its held text has no sunset or termination provision. EO 11737 (1973) rewrote Sections 2 and 5, changed the State list in Section 3(3) and inserted a new international-coordination section, redesignating Section 6 as Section 7. First end: Section 5(b) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11659, as amended, among the orders revoked effective January 1, 1982, so the revocation took effect on 1982-01-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on December 31, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. THE PRESIDENT 8933
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11841
Am ending E xecutive O rder N o. 10973,1  R elating to Adm inistration o f
Foreign Assistance and R elated Functions, to Provide fo r a D evelop­
ment C oordination Com m ittee
By virtue o f the authority vested in me by the Foreign Assistance A ct 
o f 1961, as am ended, and section 301 o f title 3 o f the U nited States 
Code, and as President o f the U nited States, it is hereby ordered as 
follow s:
Executive O rder N o. 10973 o f N ovem ber 3, 1961, as amended, is 
hereby amended by adding at the end o f Part III a new section 306, 
as follow s:
“ Sec . 306. Development Coordination Committee,  (a ) In accordance 
with section 640B o f the act, there is hereby established a Development 
Coordination Committee (hereinafter referred to as the C om m ittee). 
The Committee shall consist o f the Administrator o f the Agency for 
International Developm ent, w ho shall be Chairm an; the U nder Secre­
tary o f State for E conom ic A ffairs; the U nder Secretary o f the Treasury 
for M onetary A ffairs; the U nder Secretary o f Com m erce; the Under 
Secretary o f Agriculture; the U nder Secretary o f L abor; the Special 
Representative for Trade Negotiations; an Associate D irector o f the 
Office o f M anagement and Budget; the Executive D irector o f the Coun­
cil on International E conom ic P olicy; a representative o f the Assistant 
to the President for national security affairs; the President o f the Export- 
Import Bank o f the U nited States; and the President o f the Overseas 
Private Investment Corporation.
“ (b) W henever matters within the jurisdiction o f the Committee may 
be o f interest to Federal agencies not represented on the Committee 
under paragraph (a ) o f this section, the Chairman o f the Committee 
may consult with such agencies and may invite them to designate repre­
sentatives to participate in meetings and deliberations o f the Committee.
“ (c) U nder the foreign policy guidance o f the Secretary o f State, the 
Committee shall advise the President with respect to coordination o f 
United States policies and programs affecting the development o f the 
developing countries, including programs o f bilateral and multilateral 
development assistance.
“ (d) A ll agencies and officers o f the Government shall keep the Com ­
mittee inform ed in necessary detail as to the policies, programs, and 
activities referred to in paragraph ( c )  o f this Section.
“ (e) Nothing herein shall be deemed to derogate from  the responsi­
bilities o f the Secretary o f State, the Secretary o f the Treasury, or from  
responsibilities vested elsewhere by law or other Executive orders.”
T h e W h it e H o u se,
February 28,1975

F ield  O rganization
By virtue of the authority vested in  
me by section 1 of the act of August 1,  
1914, 38 Stat. 623 (19 U. S. C. 2), and in  
the interest of the internal management  
of the Government, it is ordered that the  
following changes be, and they are  
hereby, made in the customs field organi­
zation :
1. Neah Bay, Washington, is desig­
nated as a customs port of entry in Cus­
toms Collection District Number 30  
(Washington).
2. The designation of Guayanilla,  
Puerto Rico, as a customs port of entry  
in Customs Collection District Number  
49 (Puerto Rico) is revoked.
3. The name of the customs port of  
entry of Sonoyta, Arizona, in Customs  
Collection District Number 26 (Arizona),  
is changed to “Lukeville, Arizona.”
4. The limits of the customs port of  
entry of Lawrence, Massachusetts, in  
Customs Collection District Number 4  
(Massachusetts), are extended to include  
the Township of North Andover, County  
of Essex, State of Massachusetts.
This order shall become effective on  
the thirtieth day following the date  
hereof.
H arry  S. T ruman

SUBCHAPTER C— THE NATIONAL WILDLIFE  
REFUGE SYSTEM
PART 32— HUNTING
Wapanocca National Wildlife Refuge,  
Ark.
Notice is hereby given that pursuant 
to the authority vested in the Secretary 
of the Interior by the Migratory Bird 
Conservation Act of February 18, 1929, 
as amended (45 Stat. 1222,16 U.S.C. 715), 
and the Endangered Species Preservation 
Act of October 15, 1966 (80 Stat. 926, 
16 U.S.C. 668aa), it is proposed to amend 
50 CFR 32.11 by the addition o f Wapa­
nocca National Wildlife Refuge, Ark., 
to the list of areas open to the hunting 
of migratory game birds, as legislatively 
permitted.
It has been determined that the regu­
lated hunting of migratory game birds 
may be permitted as designated on Wa­
panocca National Wildlife Refuge with­
out detriment to the objectives for which 
the area was established.
Notice and public procedure on this 
amendment are deemed contrary to the 
public interest because of the proximity
of the migratory game bird season in 
the State of Arkansas. Since the amend­
ment benefits the public by allowing 
migratory game bird hunting on Wapa­
nocca National Wildlife Refuge, it shall 
become effective upon publication in the 
F ederal  R egister .
Section 32.11 is amended by the addi­
tion of the following area as one where 
hunting of migratory game birds is 
authorized :-
§ 32.11 List of open areas; migratory  
game birds.
* * * * *
A r k a n s a s
W APANOCCA N A T IO N A L W ILD LIFE  REFUGE 
* * * * *
John  S. G ottschalk , 
Director, Bureau of  
Sport Fisheries and Wildlife.
A ugust  17,1967.

PART 32— HUNTING
Washita National Wildlife Refuqe,  
Okla.
The following special regulation is 
issued and is effective on date of publica­
tion in the F ederal R egister .
§32.22 Special regulations;  upland  
game; for individual wildlife refuge  
areas.
Oklahoma
WASHITA NATIONAL WILDLIFE REFUGE
The public hunting of quail and rabbits 
on the Washita National Wildlife Refuge, 
Okla., is permitted only on the areas 
designated by signs as open to hunting. 
This open area, comprising 1,560 acres, is 
delineated on maps available at refuge 
headquarters, Butler, Okla., and from 
the Regional Director, Bureau of Sport 
Fisheries and Wildlife, Post Office Box 
1306, Albuquerque, N. Mex. 87103.
Upland game hunting shall be in ac­
cordance with all applicable State regu­
lations governing the hunting of quail 
and rabbits subject to the following 
special conditions:
Cl) The open season for quail hunting 
on the refuge extends from November 20, 
1967, through January 15,1968, inclusive.
(2) The open season for rabbit hunt­
ing on the refuge extends from Novem­
ber 20, 1967, through January 15, 1968, 
inclusive. Hunting will be permitted only 
on Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays, and 
national holidays.
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 32, NO. 162— TUESDAY, AUGUST 22, 1967

(3 ) All authority which was vested in the Director of the Office of

sioner of Education of disaster relief assistance for educational purposes), 
and which was transferred to the President by Reorganization Plan No 1  
of 1973.
(4 ) All authority vested in the Office of Emergency Preparedness 
or the Director thereof, including serving as Chairman of the National 
Council on Federal Disaster Assistance, by Executive Order No. 11526 
of April 22,1970.
(5 ) All authority vested in the Director of the Office of Emergency 
Preparedness by Executive Order No. 11678 of August 16, 1972, relating 
to the administration of certain temporary disaster relief provisions, and

Washington, Tuesday, November 23, 1954
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10577
Amending  the C ivil  S ervice R ules and
Authorizing  a New  A ppointment
System  for the  C ompetitive  S ervice
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by the Constitution, by section 1753 
of the Revised Statutes (5 U. S. C. 631), 
by the Civil Service Act of January 16, 
1883 (22 Stat. 403), by section 301*of title 
3 of the United States Code, and as 
President of the United States, it is here­
by ordered as follows:
P art I —Civil  S ervice R ules
Section  101. The Civil Service Rules 
are hereby amended to read as follows:
RULE I— COVERAGE AND DEFINITIONS
Sec. 1.1 Positions and employees af­
fected by these Rules.  These Rules shall 
apply to all positions in the competitive 
service and to all incumbents of such 
positions. Except as expressly provided 
in the Rule concerned, these Rules shall 
not apply to positions and employees in 
the excepted service.
Sec. 1.2 Extent of the competitive  
service. The competitive service shall 
include: (a) All civilian positions in the 
executive branch of the Government un­
less specifically excepted therefrom by 
or pursuant to statute or by the Civil 
Service Commission (hereafter referred 
to in these Rules as the Commission) 
under section 6.1 of Rule VI; and (b) 
all positions in the legislative and judi­
cial branches of the Federal Government 
and in the Government of the District 
of Columbia which are specifically made 
subject to the civil-service laws by stat­
ute. The Commission is authorized and 
directed to determine finally whether a 
position is in the competitive service.
Sec. 1.3 Definitions.  As used in these 
Rules:
(a) “Competitive service” shall have 
the same meaning as the words “clas­
sified service”, or “classified (competi­
tive) service”, or “classified civil service” 
as defined in existing statutes and exec­
utive orders.
(b) “Competitive position” shall mean 
a position in the competitive service.
(c) “Competitive status” shall mean 
basic eligibility to be noncompetitively
selected to fill a vacancy in a competi­
tive position. A competitive status shall 
be acquired by career-conditional or 
career appointment through open com­
petitive examination upon satisfactory 
completion of a probationary period, or 
may be granted by statute, executive or­
der, or the Civil Service Rules without 
competitive examination. A person with 
competitive status may be promoted,

RULE II— APPOINTMENT THROUGH THE  
COMPETITIVE SYSTEM
Sec. 2.1 Competitive examinations  
and eligible registers,  (a) The Commis­
sion shall be responsible for open com­
petitive examinations for admission to 
the competitive service which will fairly 
test the relative capacity and fitness of 
the persons examined for the position to 
be filled. The Commission is author­
ized to establish standards with respect 
to citizenship, age, education, training 
and experience, suitability, and physical 
and mental fitness, and for residence or 
other requirements which applicants 
must meet to be admitted to or rated in 
examinations.
(b) In addition to the names of per­
sons who qualify in competitive exami­
nations, the names of persons who have 
lost eligibility on a career or career-con­
ditional register because of service in the 
armed forces, and the names of persons 
who lost opportunity for certification or 
who have served under career or career- 
conditional appointment when the Com­
mission determines that they should be 
given certification, may also be entered 
at such places on appropriate registers 
and under such conditions as the Com­
mission may prescribe.
S ec. 2.2 Appointments,  (a) The 
Commission shall establish and admin­
ister a career-conditional appointment 
system for positions subject to competi­
tive examination which will permit ad­
justment of the career service to 
necessary fluctuations in Federal em- 
•  ployment, and provide an equitable and 
orderly system for stabilizing the Fed­
eral work force. A competitive status 
shall be acquired by a career-conditional 
appointee upon satisfactory completion 
of a probationary period, but the ap­
pointee shall have career-conditional 
tenure for a period of service to be pre­
scribed by regulation of the Commission.7545

RULE IV— PROHIBITED PRACTICES
Sec. 4.1 Prohibition against political  
activity.  No person employed in the 
executive branch of the Federal Govern­
ment, or any agency or department 
thereof, shall use his official authority or 
influence for the purpose of interfering 
with an election or affecting the result 
thereof. No person occupying a posi­
tion in the competitive service shall take 
any active part in political management 
or in political campaigns, except as may 
be provided by or pursuant to statute. 
All such persons shall retain the right to
vote as they may choose and to express 
•  their opinions on all political subjects 
and candidates.
Sec. 4.2 Prohibitigri against racial,  
political or religious discrimination.  No 
person employed in the executive branch 
of the Federal Government who has au­
thority to take or recommend any per­
sonnel action with respect to any person 
who is an employee in the competitive 
service or any eligible or applicant for a 
position in the competitive service shall 
make any inquiry concerning the race, 
political affiliation or religious beliefs of 
any such employee, eligible, or applicant. 
All disclosures concerning such matters 
shall be ignored, except as to such mem­
bership in political parties or organiza­
tions as constitutes by law a disqualifica­
tion for Government employment. No 
discrimination shall be exercised, threat­
ened, or promised by any person in the 
executive branch of the Federal Govern­
ment against or in favor of any employee 
in the competitive service, or any eligible 
or applicant for a position in the com­
petitive service because of his race, 
political affiliation or religious beliefs, 
except as may be authorized or required 
by law.
Sec. 4.3 Prohibition against securing  
withdrawal from competition.  No per­
son shall influence another person to 
withdraw from competition for any posi­
tion in the competitive service for the 
purpose of either improving or injuring 
the prospects of any applicant for ap­
pointment. The Commission is author­
ized to take such disciplinary action as 
it deems appropriate whenever it finds 
that any person has violated this section.

mission is authorized and directed to

as may be necessary to carry out the pro­
visions of the Civil Service Act and Rules, 
the Veterans’  Preference Act, and all 
other applicable statutes or .executive 
orders imposing responsibilities on the 
Commission.
(b) The Commission is authorized, 
whenever there shall be practical diffi­
culties and unnecessary hardships in 
complying with the strict letter of its 
regulations, to grant a variation from the 
strict letter of the regulations if such 
variation is within the spirit of the regu­
lations, and the efficiency of the Govern­
ment and the integrity of the competi­

tion is granted the Commission shall

(3) the circumstances which protect or 
promote the efficiency of the Government 
and the integrity of the competitive serv­
ice, and (4) a statement limiting the 
application of the variation to the con­
tinuation of the conditions which gave 
rise to the variation: Provided further,  
That similar variations shall be granted 
whenever similar conditions exist. All

Sec. 6.1 Authority to except positions  
from the competitive service,  (a) The 
Commission is authorized to except posi­
tions from the competitive service when­
ever it determines th at appointments 
thereto through competitive examina­
tion are not practicable. Upon the rec­
ommendation of the agency concerned,

schedule.

Schedule C.  Positions of a confidential or  
policy-determining character shall be listed

sitions and status of incumbents,  (a)

ments and position changes in the ex­
cepted service shall be made in accord­
ance with such regulations and practices

cepted positions.  Except as may be

Washington, Tuesday, February 21, 1950
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10110
P resid en t’s C o m m unications P olicy  
B oard
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me as President of the United States, 
it is hereby ordered as follows :
1. There is hereby created a board to 
be known as the President’ s Communi­
cations Policy Board which shall be com­
posed of a chairman and four other 
members to be designated by the Presi­
dent.
2. It shall be the function of the Board 
to study the present and potential use 
of radio and wire communications facili­
ties by governmental and non-govern­
mental agencies and to make and present 
to the President evaluations and recom­
mendations in the national interest con­
cerning (a) policies for the most effective 
use of radio frequencies by governmental 
and non-governmental users and alter­
native administrative arrangements in 
the Federal Government for the sound 
effectuation of such policies, (b) policies 
with respect to international radio and 
wire communications, (c) the relation­
ship of Government communications to 
non-government communications, and 
(d) such related policy matters as the 
Board may determine.
3. The Board is authorized to hear and 
consult with representatives of industry 
and the Federal Government concerned 
with the subjects under study by the 
Board. All executive departments and 
agencies of the Federal Government are 
authorized and directed to cooperate with 
the Board in its work and to furnish the 
Board such information as it may re­
quire in the performance of its duties. 
The Board shall protect the security of 
any classified information submitted to 
it.
4. Each member of the Board shall, 
while away from his home or regular 
place of business and engaged in the 
official business of the Board, receive 
actual traveling expenses and per diem 
allowances in lieu of subsistence in ac­
cordance with rates established by the 
Standardized Government Travel Reg­
ulations, as amended.
5. During the fiscal year 1950 the ex­
penditures of the Board and the travel-
ing expenses and per diem allowances 
of the members thereof shall be paid out 
of an allotment made by the President 
from the appropriation appearing under 
the heading “Emergency Fund for the 
President” in the Independent Offices 
Appropriation Act, 1950 (Public Law 266, 
approved August 24, 1949); and during 
the fiscal year 1951 the same shall be 
similarly paid from any corresponding 
or like appropriation made available for 
the fiscal year 1951. Such payments 
shall be made without regard to the 
provisions of (a) section 3681 of the Re­
vised Statutes (31 U. S. C. 672), (b) sec­
tion 9 of the act of March 4, 1909, 35 
Stat. 1027 (31 U. S. C. 673), and (c) 
such other laws as the President may 
hereafter specify.
The Board shall terminate one year 
after the date of this order.
H arry  S. T ruman

February 17,1950.

By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by the Act of this date, entitled “An 
Act to authorize the President to extend 
enlistments in the Armed Forces of the 
United States,” and as President of the 
United States and Commander in Chief 
of the armed forces of the United States, 
I hereby extend for a period of twelve 
months all enlistments in the Army, the 
United States Navy, and the United 
States Marine Corps, including the Naval 
Reserve and the Marine Corps Reserve, 
and in any component of the Air Force 
of the United States, which shall expire 
at any time after the date of this order 
and prior to July 9,1951: Provided, That 
nothing contained herein shall be con­
strued to prevent voluntary re-enlist­
ments or voluntary extension of existing 
enlistments under provisions of applica­
ble laws or the regulations of the De­
partments of the Army, Navy and Air 
Force.

directed to take such steps as he may 
deem necessary to carry out the provi­
sions of this order.

Thursday, October 25, 1962 FEDERAL REGISTER 10403
Executive Order 11058
ASSIGNING AUTHORITY WITH RESPECT TO ORDERING PERSONS AND  
UNITS IN THE READY RESERVE TO ACTIVE DUTY AND WITH RESPECT  
TO EXTENSION OF ENLISTMENTS AND OTHER PERIODS OF SERVICE  
IN THE ARMED FORCES
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Joint Resolution of 
October 3,1962 (Public Law 87-736), and by section 301 of title 3 of 
the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it is 
hereby ordered as follows:
S ection 1. The Secretary of Defense, and, when designated by him 
for this purpose, any of the Secretaries of the military departments of 
the Department of Defense, and the Secretary of the Treasury with 
respect to the Coast Guard are hereby authorized and empowered to 
exercise the authority vested in the President until February 28,1963, 
by section 1 of the Act of October 3, 1962 (Public Law 87-736) to 
order, without the consent of the persons concerned, any unit, or any 
member, of the Ready Reserve of an armed force to active duty for 
not more than twelve consecutive months, provided there are not more 
than 150,000 members of the Ready Reserve thereby on active duty 
(other than for training) without their consent at any one time.
S ec. 2. In  pursuance of the provisions of section 2 of the said 
Joint Resolution of October 3, 1962, the Secretary of Defense and 
the Secretary of the Treasury with respect to the Coast Guard are 
hereby authorized to extend enlistments, appointments, periods of 
active duty, periods of active duty for training, periods of obligated 
service or other military status in any component of an armed force 
or in the National Guard that expire before February 28, 1963, for 
not more than twelve months. However, if the enlistment of a 
member of the ^  Ready Reserve who is ordered to active duty under 
section 1 of this Executive Order would expire after February 28, 
1963, but before he has served the entire period for which he was so 
ordered to active duty, his enlistment may be extended until theTast 
day of that period.
S ec. 3. In  pursuance of the provisions of section 3 of the said Joint 
Resolution of October 3, 1962, no member of the armed forces who 
was involuntarily ordered to active duty or whose period of active 
duty was extended under the Act of August 1, 1961, Public Law 
87-117 (75 Stat. 242), may be involuntarily ordered to active duty 
under this Executive Order.
J o h n F. K ennedy
T h e W h it e H ouse,
October 23, 1962.

Thursday, October 25, 1962 FEDERAL REGISTER 10405
Executive Order 11059
DESIGNATING PUBLIC INTERNATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS ENTITLED
TO ENJOY CERTAIN PRIVILEGES, EXEMPTIONS, AND IMMUNITIES
W HEREAS the Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission is an 
international organization in which the United States participates 
pursuant to the Convention with Costa Rica for the Establishment 
of an Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission, May 31, 1949, 1 
UST 230, TIAS 2044; and
W HEREAS the Great Lakes Fishery Commission is an inter­
national organization in which the United States participates pur­
suant to the Convention with Canada for the Establishment of a 
Great Lakes Fishery Commission, September 10, 1954, 6 UST 2836; 
TIAS 3326; and
W HEREAS the International Pacific Halibut Commission is an 
international organization in which the United States participates 
pursuant to the Convention with Canada for the Preservation of the 
Halibut Fishery of the Northern Pacific Ocean and Bering Sea, 
I ,  March 2, 1953, 5 UST 5; TIAS 2900, being the last of a series of
similar treaties dating from 1923:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 1 of the International Organizations Immunities Act (59 
Stat. 669; 22 U.S.C. 288), I hereby designate the Inter-American 
Tropical Tuna Commission, the Great Lakes Fishery Commission, 
and the International Pacific Halibut Commission as public inter­
national organizations entitled to enjoy the privileges, exemptions, 
and immunities conferred by the International Organizations Im ­
munities Act, except those conferred pursuant to Sections 4(b), 4(e), 
and 5 (a) of that Act.
The designation of the above-named international organizations as 
public international organizations within the meaning of the Inter­
national Organizations Immunities Act is not intended to abridge in 
any respect privileges, exemptions, and immunities which these 
organizations may have acquired or may acquire by treaty or con­
gressional action.
J ohn  F. K ennedy

By virtue of and pursuant to the 
authority vested in me by section 201 (e) 
of the Career Compensation Act of 1949,
approved October 12, 1949 (Public Law 
351, 81st Congress), and as President of 
the United States and Commander in 
Chief of the armed forces of the United 
States, I  hereby prescribe the following 
regulations relating to the inclusion as 
active duty of time required for travel 
from home to first duty station and from 
last duty station to home by members of 
the uniformed services called or ordered 
to active duty in excess of thirty days :
S ection  1. In case travel by public 
transportation is authorized, the travel 
time included as active duty shall be 
based upon actual and necessary sched­
ules which most nearly coincide with the 
possible time of departure and arrival by 
the mode of transportation actually 
used, or by public surface transportation 
if the travel is actually performed by 
private conveyance without having been 
specifically authorized.
S ec. 2. In case travel by private con­
veyance is specifically authorized and 
the travel is so performed, thé travel time 
included as active duty shall be com­
puted on the basis of one day for each 
three hundred miles traveled, and one 
day of travel time shall also be allowed 
for each fraction of three hundred miles 
in excess of one hundred and fifty miles.
The distance traveled shall be computed 
on the basis of distances established by 
the official mileage tables in use by the 
uniformed services. Travel by private 
conveyance shall not be specifically au­
thorized in any case in which the call to 
active duty is for a period of less than 
ninety consecutive days.
S ec. 3. The Secretaries concerned 
(within the meaning of section 102 (f) 
of the said Career Compensation Act of 
1949) may prescribe with respect to per­
sonnel of the uniformed services within 
their respective departments or agency 
such supplementary regulations not 
inconsistent herewith as they may deem 
necessary or desirable for carrying out 
these regulations, and such supplemen­
tary regulations shall be uniform for all 
the services to the fullest extent prac­
ticable.
S ec. 4. This order shall become effec­
tive on September 1, 1950.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the Defense Production 
Act of 1950, as amended (64 Stat. 798; 50 U .S.C  App. 2061, e t seq .)  
and section 301 of title 3, United States Code, and as Commander in Chief 
of the Armed Forces of the United States, it is hereby ordered as follows
PART 1 — PURPOSE, POLICY AND IMPLEMENTATION
Section 101. P u rp o se. This order delegates authorities and addresses national 
defense industrial resource policies and programs under the Defense Produc­
tion Act of 1950, as amended (“the A ct”), except for the amendments to 
Title III of the Act in the Energy Security Act of 1980 and telecommunication 
authorities under Executive Order No. 12472.
Sec. 102. P o licy . The United States must have an industrial and technology 
base capable of meeting national defense requirements, and capable of con­
tributing to the technological superiority o f its defense equipment in peace­
time and in times of national emergency. The domestic industrial and techno- 
logical base is the foundation for national defense preparedness. The authori­
ties provided in the Act shall be used to strengthen this base and to ensure 
it is capable of responding to all threats to the national security of the 
United States.
Sec. 103. G en era l F u n ctio n s.  Federal departments and agencies responsible 
for defense acquisition (or for industrial resources needed to support defense 
acquisition) shall:
(a) Identify requirements for the full spectrum of national security emer­
gencies, including m ilitary, industrial, and essential civilian demand;
(b) Assess continually the capability of the domestic industrial and techno­
logical base to satisfy requirements in peacetime and times of national 
emergency, specifically evaluating the availability o f adequate industrial 
resource and production sources, including subcontractors and suppliers 
materials, skilled labor, and professional and technical personnel;
(c) Be prepared, in the event of a potential threat to the security of 
the United States, to take actions necessary to ensure the availability of 
adequate industrial resources and production capability, including services 
and critical technology for national defense requirements;
(d) Improve the efficiency and responsiveness to defense requirements 
of the domestic industrial base; and
(e) Foster cooperation between the defense and commercial sectors for 
research and development and for acquisition of materials, components 
and equipment to enhance industrial base efficiency and responsiveness
Sec. 104. Im p le m e n ta tio n , (a) The National Security Council is the principal 
forum for consideration and resolution of national security resource prepared­
ness policy. -
(b) The Director, Federal Emergency' Management Agency (“Director 
FEM A”) shall:
(1) Serve as an advisor to the National Security Council on issues 
of national security resource preparedness and on the use of the 
authorities and functions delegated by this order-

(c) The head of every Federal department and agency assigned functions

PART H— PRtORITIES AND ALLOCATIONS
Sec. 2G T. Delegations of Priorities and Allocations,  (a) The authority of  
the President conferred by section 101 of the Act to require acceptance  
and priority performance of contracts or orders (other than contracts of  
employment) to promote the national defense over performance of any other  
contracts or orders, and to allocate materials, services, and facilities as  
deemed necessary or appropriate to promote the national defense, is delegated  
to the following agency heads;
(1) The Secretary of Agriculture with respect to food resources,  
food resource facilities, and the domestic distribution of farm equip­
ment and commercial fertilizer;.
(2) The Secretary of Energy with respect to all forms of energy;
(3) The Secretary of Health and Human Services with respect to  
health resources;
(4) The Secretary of Transportation with respect to all forms of  
civil transportation;
(5) ;  The Secretary of Defense with respect to water resources; and
(6) The Secretary of Commerce for all other materials, services,  
and facilities, including construction materials.
C & l f  The Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the heads of those  
departments and agencies specified in subsection 201(a) of this order, shall  
administer the Defense Priorities and Allocations System (“DPAS”) regula­
tions that will be used to implement the authority of the President conferred  
by section 1-01 of the Act as delegated to the Secretary of Commerce in  
subsection 201(a)(6) of this order. The Secretary of Commerce will redelegate  
to the-Secretary of Defense, and the heads of other departments and agencies  
as appropriate, authority for the priority rating of contracts and orders for  
all. materials, services, and facilities needed in support of programs approved  
under section 202 of this order. The Secretary of Commerce shall act as  
appropriate upon Special Priorities Assistance requests in a time frame  
consistent with the urgency of the need at hand.
fcl The Director, FEMA, shall attempt to resolve issues or disagreements  
on priorities or allocations between Federal departments or agencies in  
a time frame consistent with the urgency of the issue at hand and, if  
not resolved, such issues will be referred to the Assistant to the President  
for National Security Affairs for final determination.
(dr) The head of each Federal department or agency assigned functions  
under subsection 201(a) of this order, when necessary, shall make the finding  
required under subsection 101(b) of the Act. This finding shall be submitted  
for the President’s approval through the Assistant to the President for Na­
tional Security Affairs. Upon such approval the head, of the Federal depart-

Sec. 202. Determinations.  The authority delegated by section 201 of this 
order may be used only to support programs that have been determined 
in writing as necessary or appropriate to promote the national defense:
(a) By the Secretary of Defense with respect to military production and 
construction, military assistance to foreign nations, stockpiling, outer space, 
and directly related activities;
(b) By the Secretary of Energy with respect to energy production and 
construction, distribution and use, and directly related activities; and
(c) By the Director, FEMA, with respect to essential civilian needs support­
ing national defense, including civil defense and continuity of government 
and directly related activities.
Sec. 203. Maximizing Domestic  Energy Supplies.  The authority of the Presi­
dent to perform the functions provided by subsection 101(c) of the Act 
is delegated to the Secretary of Commerce, who shall redelegate to the 
Secretary of Energy the authority to make the findings described in subsection 
101(c)(2)(A) that the m aterials (including equipment), services, and facilities 
are critical and essential. The Secretary of Commerce shall make the finding 
described in subsection 101(c)(2)(A) of the Act that the materials (including 
equipment), services, or facilities are scarce, and the finding described in 
subsection 101(c)(2)(B) that it is necessary to use the authority provided 
by subsection 101(c)(1).
Sec. 204. Chemical and Biological Warfare.  The authority of the President 
conferred by subsection 104(b) of the Act is delegated to the Secretary 
of Defense. This authority may not be further delegated by the Secretary.
PART III— EXPANSION OF PRODUCTIVE CAPACITY AND SUPPLY
Sec. 301. (a) Financing Institution Guarantees.  To expedite or expand produc­
tion and deliveries or services under government contracts for the procure­
ment of industrial resources or critical technology items essential to the 
national defense, the head of each Federal department or agency engaged 
in procurement for the national defense (referred to as “agency head” in 
this part) and the President and Chairman o f the Export-Import Bank of 
the United States (in cases involving capacity expansion, technological d evel­
opment, or production in foreign countries) are authorized to guarantee 
in w hole or in part any public or private financing institution, subject 
to provisions of section 301 of the Act. Guarantees shall be made in consulta­
tion with the Department of the Treasury as to the terms and conditions 
thereof. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget (“OMB”) 
shall be informed when such guarantees are to be made.
(b) Direct Loan Guarantees.  To expedite or expand production and deliv­
eries or services under government contracts for the procurement of industrial 
resources or critical technology items essential to the national defense, each 
agency head is authorized to make direct loan guarantees from funds appro­
priated to their agency for Title HI.
(c) Fiscal Agent.  Each Federal Reserve Bank is designated and authorized 
to act, on behalf of any guaranteeing agency, as fiscal agent in the making 
of guarantee contracts and in otherwise carrying out the purposes of section 
301 of the Act.
(d) Regulations.  The Board of Governors o f the Federal Reserve System 
is authorized, after consultation with heads of guaranteeing departments 
and agencies, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Director, OMB, to
